stories.title: 3 Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stocks That Turned $10,000 Into More Than $100,000 in 5 Years (Hint: They've All Outperformed Nvidia)
stories.simple_summary: Some AI company stocks made investors a lot of money over the past 5 years, earning more than the famous Nvidia company.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: US data centers could consume more natural gas than Germany and Japan combined by 2035
stories.simple_summary: AI computers use a lot of electricity and natural gas to run. By 2035, U.S. data centers might use more natural gas than entire countries like Germany or Japan.
stories.why_it_matters: This could affect your electric and heating bills if energy prices go up because of all this AI demand.

stories.title: Poway City Council to consider AI data centers ban
stories.simple_summary: A city council in Poway is thinking about banning new AI data centers from being built there.
stories.why_it_matters: If you live in Poway, this could affect local jobs and development plans in your area.

stories.title: Opinion | Don’t let AI build the next AI
stories.simple_summary: An opinion piece argues that humans should have more control over building new AI systems instead of letting AI build AI.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a debate about the direction of AI technology — not something that changes your life immediately.

stories.title: AI agents now have a place to snitch
stories.simple_summary: Companies created a hotline where AI systems can report problems they see, like a tip line for artificial intelligence.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to engineers and companies — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: Meta expands subscription push with new AI-focused plans
stories.simple_summary: Meta (which owns Facebook and Instagram) is selling a new subscription plan that gives you extra AI features along with ad-free social media.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use Facebook, Instagram, or WhatsApp, Meta wants you to pay monthly for better features and more AI help.

stories.title: Trump facing AI backlash in Congress as push for guardrails intensifies
stories.simple_summary: Congress is pushing back on a plan to speed up AI development without safety rules.
stories.why_it_matters: This is about government policy — it may eventually affect how safe AI tools are for you to use.

stories.title: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google have been in talks on AI safety for weeks
stories.simple_summary: Three big AI companies held meetings to discuss how to make AI safer, while some government leaders want to skip safety rules to compete with China.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a behind-the-scenes debate among tech leaders and government — nothing you need to do right now.

stories.title: AEO startup Profound hits unicorn valuation, raises $180M Series D 7 months after last round
stories.simple_summary: A startup company that works with AI just raised a huge amount of money and is now worth $1.8 billion.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: Meta’s new One subscriptions put a price on social media and AI
stories.simple_summary: Meta is now selling subscription plans that bundle ad-free social media with access to extra AI features.
stories.why_it_matters: If you want to use more of Meta's AI tools or remove ads from Facebook and Instagram, you'll need to pay a monthly fee.

stories.title: Former TikTok execs built an app that uses AI to teach you how to pose for a photo
stories.simple_summary: A new camera app uses AI to suggest better poses for your photos, like having a photographer guide you.
stories.why_it_matters: If you take a lot of photos or selfies, this is just a fun new tool to try — not necessary for your life.

stories.title: Discover how to take your startup from prototype to production at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
stories.simple_summary: A tech conference is advertising a speaking event for people who want to learn how to grow their startups.
stories.why_it_matters: Only relevant if you're starting a business and want to attend a conference — not for most people.
